title: Review: Capacitance and capacitor energy; Potential difference and emf; Charge and current
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EL01-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; EL01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; EL09-2#t2 term and clue written for the game; EL01-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EL01-1#N.11, EL02-1#N.9, EL09-1#N.5, EL09-2#N.3, EL09-3#N.4, EL01-1#N.6b, EL02-1#N.13c, EL09-1#N.2, EL09-2#N.13a, EL01-1#N.3, EL02-1#N.6, EL01-1#N.12. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Current
items.clue: Rate of flow of charge through a cross-section.

items.label: Coulomb
items.clue: Unit: the amount passing a place in a wire when 1 A flows for 1 s.

items.label: Capacitance
items.clue: Quantity for parallel plates that is proportional to area A and to 1/d.

items.label: Free electrons
items.clue: Carriers already present throughout a metal wire, moving opposite to the conventional way.

questions.stem: Several wires meet at a junction in a circuit with steady currents. A student measures a current of 1.20 A in one wire leading into the junction, and currents of 0.70 A and 0.40 A in two wires leading out of it. The ammeters are ideal and read correctly. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: The other wires at the junction carry a net current of 0.10 A away from it.
0.10 A of the current was used up as charge passed through the junction.
Charge is building up at the junction at a rate of 0.10 C each second.
An unmeasured wire must carry 2.30 A, the sum of the three measured currents.

questions.stem: For two points A and B in an electric field, V_B − V_A = −50 V. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A charged object moved from A to B changes U_E by −50 J, whatever its charge
A −1.0 C charge moved from A to B lowers U_E by 50 J, as B is at lower potential
U_E falls by 50 J per coulomb on the straight path, and by more on a longer, curved path
If a +1.0 C charge were moved from A to B, by any path, U_E would change by −50 J

questions.stem: A parallel-plate capacitor is connected to an ideal 12 V battery. When the capacitor is fully charged, its positive plate carries a charge of 3.6 × 10⁻⁵ C. What is the capacitance of the capacitor?

An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor has a capacitance of 16 pF. A second air-filled parallel-plate capacitor has plates with three times the area of the first capacitor's plates, and its plates are twice as far apart. What is the capacitance of the second capacitor?

options.text: 96 pF
12 pF
48 pF
24 pF

questions.stem: Four identical capacitors, each of capacitance C, are first connected all in parallel, giving an equivalent capacitance C_X. They are then reconnected all in series, giving an equivalent capacitance C_Y. How does C_X compare with C_Y?

options.text: C_X is 1/16 times C_Y.
C_X is 4 times C_Y.
C_X is the same as C_Y.
C_X is 16 times C_Y.

questions.stem: A copper wire carries a current directed toward the right. Which statement describes the motion of the charge carriers that make up this current?

options.text: Positive ions drift toward the right, while the free electrons stay in their places.
Free electrons drift toward the left, while the positive ions drift toward the right.
Free electrons drift toward the left, while the positive ions stay in their places.
Free electrons drift toward the right, the same direction as the conventional current.

questions.stem: A 12 V battery moves 60 C of charge through a starter motor. How much energy does it transfer to that charge?
questions.explanation: The battery gives each coulomb 12 J: energy = qε = 60 C × 12 J/C = 720 J.

questions.stem: Predict first. An uncharged parallel-plate capacitor is connected to a battery and left until it is fully charged. Which statement correctly describes how the capacitor becomes charged?

options.text: Electrons move from one plate, through the wires and battery, to the other plate.
Electrons cross the gap between the two plates, from one plate to the other.
The battery creates new charge and places some on each of the two plates.
The battery adds charge to one plate, and the other plate remains neutral.

questions.stem: An air-filled parallel-plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the supply. Its plates are then pulled apart to twice their separation. What happens to the charge on each plate, the potential difference across the capacitor and the energy it stores?

options.text: Charge unchanged; potential difference doubles; energy doubles.
Charge halves; potential difference unchanged; energy halves.
Charge unchanged; potential difference halves; energy halves.
Charge, potential difference and energy are all unchanged.

questions.explanation: Disconnected, the charge has nowhere to go: Q is fixed. C ∝ 1/d halves, so the potential difference Q/C doubles and the energy ½Q²/C doubles. The extra energy is the work done pulling the attracting plates apart.

questions.stem: In an electron beam in a vacuum tube, 1.5 × 10¹⁵ electrons pass through a cross-section of the beam in 8.0 s at a steady rate. What is the magnitude of the current in the beam? Use e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
Predict first. A cell has an emf of 1.5 V. What does this mean?

options.text: The cell holds a store of 1.5 C of charge, which it releases into the circuit.
The cell pushes each coulomb of charge around the circuit with a force of 1.5 N.
For each coulomb passing through the cell, 1.5 J is transferred to electrical energy.
The cell drives a current of 1.5 A through any circuit connected to it.

questions.stem: A copper wire has a thick section X joined to a thin section Y, and there is a steady current in the wire. How do the currents I_X and I_Y in the two sections compare?

options.text: They are equal: the same charge passes each cross-section per second.
I_Y is greater, since the charges move faster through the narrow section Y.
I_X is greater, since the thick section X holds more of the charge carriers.
It depends on the direction of the current, as current decreases along a wire.
